sources.label: NSCP 2015 (National Structural Code of the Philippines), Chapter 2 — Seismic Provisions
sources.description: Classifies Philippine seismic zones. Most of the Philippines is Seismic Zone 4. Provides seismic load parameters.

sources.label: NSCP 2015, Table 304.1 — Presumptive Allowable Bearing Capacities
sources.description: Provides presumptive bearing capacities: Crystalline bedrock 600 kPa, Sedimentary rock 300 kPa, Well-cemented gravel/sand-gravel 300 kPa, Medium-dense sand/silty sand 100 kPa, Stiff clay 100 kPa, Medium-stiff clay 50 kPa.

sources.label: NSCP 2015, Section 304.2 — Minimum Footing and Bearing Capacity Increase
sources.description: Minimum footing 300mm width × 300mm depth into natural grade. 20% bearing capacity increase for each additional 300mm of width/depth, up to 3x the base value.

sources.label: PD 1096 RIRR 2004, Rule III — Geotechnical Investigation Requirements
sources.description: Requires mandatory soil boring, load tests, and written geotechnical report from licensed civil/geotechnical engineer submitted with building permit application.

sources.label: PHIVOLCS Fault Buffer Zone Recommendation — 5m from Active Fault Trace
sources.description: DOST-PHIVOLCS recommends minimum 5m buffer zone from both sides of active fault trace or edge of deformation zone. No permanent structures allowed within this zone.

sources.label: PHIVOLCS Liquefcation Susceptibility and Ground Shaking Hazard Maps
sources.description: PHIVOLCS-produced liquefaction susceptibility maps document risk areas. Loose sandy/silty soil with high water table (<10m), reclaimed land, alluvial plains, and river proximity indicate susceptibility.
